title: Can you make a top-level class private?
shortTitle: Can you make a class private?
keyPoints: A top-level class CANNOT be private or protected – only public or package-private (default)
A nested/inner class CAN be private – visible only to its enclosing class
Private nested classes are used for implementation details: cache, node, builder internals
Understanding this concept is essential for Java interviews at senior level
This concept directly affects how banking applications manage resources

s1_definition.oneliner: A top-level class cannot be private (compiler error). A nested class can be private, visible only to its enclosing class.
s1_definition.profdef:
Access rules for classes:

- **Top-level:** Only `public` or default (package-private). `private class X {}` at top level does not compile.
- **Nested/inner:** All four modifiers work: `public`, `protected`, default, `private`.
- **Private nested:** Used for internal implementation classes like cache entries, linked list nodes, builder internals.
s1_definition.analogy: A bank branch (top-level class) is either open to the public or known within the district (package-private). But a room inside the branch (nested class) can be private – like the vault, accessible only to the branch itself.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Top-level class:   public or default (no modifier)
                     private → COMPILE ERROR
                     protected → COMPILE ERROR

  Nested/inner class: all four modifiers allowed
                     private = visible only to enclosing class
                     Used for: cache entries, nodes, builder internals
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A top-level class cannot be private because there is no enclosing class for it to be private relative to. Only public and package-private are allowed. A nested class can use all four access modifiers, and private nested classes are commonly used for internal implementation details.

One sentence to remember: top-level classes are public or package-private – only nested classes can be private.
